method: Claude Sonnet drafting, with Claude Opus revision of passages flagged by checks; blind English back-translation by a separate agent that never saw the source; independent semantic checks against the exact English

items.sourceEnglish: Food Forest Design
items.draft: Moralo wa Moru wa Dijo
items.blindBackTranslation: Forest of Food Forest [?: "Moralo wa Moru wa Dijo" literally "Structure/Plan of the Forest of Food"]. Literal: "The Structure of the Food Forest"

items.sourceEnglish: Layer a multi-storey food system from tall canopy right down to root crops.
items.draft: Hlophisa tsamaiso ya dijo ka mekgahlelo e mengata, ho tloha ho canopy e telele ho isa ho dijalo tsa metso.
items.blindBackTranslation: Arrange the food system in many layers, from the tall canopy down to the root crops.

items.sourceEnglish: An indigenous forest fills the space from the highest branches to the roots.
items.draft: Moru wa indigenous o tlatsa sebaka ho tloha makaleng a phahameng ka ho fetisisa ho isa metsong.
items.blindBackTranslation: An indigenous forest fills the space from the highest branches down to the roots.

items.sourceEnglish: Different plants use the light and moisture available at their level.
items.draft: Dimela tse fapaneng di sebedisa kganya le mongobo tse fumanehang boemong ba tsona.
items.blindBackTranslation: Different plants use the light and moisture that are available at their position.

items.sourceEnglish: A food forest copies this pattern with productive species.
items.draft: Moru wa dijo o etsisa mokgwa ona ka mefuta ya dimela e hlahisang.
items.blindBackTranslation: A food forest imitates this way with the kinds of plants it produces.

items.sourceEnglish: The result is not one crop in one row, but many useful layers growing together.
items.draft: Sephetho ha se sejalo se le seng moleng o le mong, empa ke mekgahlelo e mengata e molemo e melang hammoho.
items.blindBackTranslation: The result is not one crop in one row, but many good layers growing together.

items.sourceEnglish: Think of tall canopy, smaller trees, shrubs and herbaceous plants.
items.draft: Nahana ka canopy e telele, difate tse nyane, dihlahla le dimela tsa herbaceous.
items.blindBackTranslation: Think of a tall canopy, small trees, shrubs and herbaceous plants.

items.sourceEnglish: Ground cover protects the surface, root crops grow below it, and climbers use suitable supports.
items.draft: Dimela tse koahelang mobu di sireletsa bokaholimo, dijalo tsa metso di hola ka tlase ho bona, mme dimela tse nyolohang di sebedisa dintho tse loketseng tseo di ka nyolohelang ho tsona.
items.blindBackTranslation: Plants that cover the ground protect the surface, root crops grow below them, and climbing plants use suitable things that they can climb up.

items.sourceEnglish: The heights and spacing depend on the plants and site. These are planning layers, not fixed height bands.
items.draft: Bophahamo le sebaka sa ho jala di itshetlehile ka dimela le sebaka. Mekgahlelo ena ke ya ho rala; ha e bolele dibaka tse tsitsitseng tsa bophahamo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Height and planting space depend on the plants and the place. These layers are for planning; they do not state fixed distances of height.

items.sourceEnglish: The original Highveld example includes Wild Fig or pecan above lemon, naartjie and black mulberry.
items.draft: Mohlala wa pele wa Highveld o kenyelletsa Wild Fig kapa pecan tse hodimo ho lemon, naartjie le black mulberry.
items.blindBackTranslation: The first Highveld example includes Wild Fig or pecan above lemon, naartjie and black mulberry.

items.sourceEnglish: It places Cape gooseberry and Wild Medlar with vegetables, wild garlic, sweet potato and granadilla.
items.draft: Mohlala oo o beha Cape gooseberry le Wild Medlar mmoho le meroho, wild garlic, sweet potato le granadilla.
items.blindBackTranslation: That example places Cape gooseberry and Wild Medlar together with vegetables, wild garlic, sweet potato and granadilla.

items.sourceEnglish: Treat this as a layout example, not permission to plant every species. Check identity, frost tolerance, mature size and local restrictions first.
items.draft: Nka sena e le mohlala wa moralo, e seng tumello ya ho jala mofuta o mong le o mong. Pele ho tsohle, hlahloba hore semela ke sefe, frost tolerance, boholo ba ho hola ka botlalo le dithibelo tsa lehae.
items.blindBackTranslation: Take this as an example of a plan, not a permission to plant every kind. Before everything, check what the plant is, frost tolerance, size of full growth and local restrictions.

items.sourceEnglish: Young plants need establishment care: moisture checks, weed control and protection from damage.
items.draft: Dimela tse nyane di hloka tlhokomelo ya ho hlongwa: ho hlahloba mongobo, ho laola dimela tse sa batleheng le ho di sireletsa ho tshenyeho.
items.blindBackTranslation: Small plants need establishment care: checking moisture, controlling unwanted plants and protecting them from damage.

items.sourceEnglish: As plants grow, shade and leaf litter change conditions below them.
items.draft: Ha dimela di ntse di hola, moriti le leaf litter di fetola maemo a ka tlase ho tsona.
items.blindBackTranslation: As plants keep growing, shade and leaf litter change the conditions beneath them.

items.sourceEnglish: Check competition and access. Prune, thin or adjust lower planting when observations call for it; the system does not become care-free on a fixed birthday.
items.draft: Hlahloba tlhodisano le phihlello. Faola, etsa thinning kapa fetola dimela tse ka tlase tse jetsweng ha seo o se bonang se bontsha hore ho hlokahala jwalo; tsamaiso ena ha e fetohe e se hlokeng tlhokomelo hobane feela selemo se behilweng se fihlile.
items.blindBackTranslation: Test the connection and the result [?: tlhodisano = connection/relationship; phihlello = success/outcome]. Prune, do thinning, or change the plants below that were sown when what you see shows that it is necessary so; this system does not change without needing attention just because the set season has arrived.

items.sourceEnglish: A food forest cross-section with a tall central tree, smaller trees, shrubs, upright plants, ground cover and a vine, with their roots branching through the soil; sunlight enters from the upper left.
items.draft: Karolo e kgaotsweng ya moru wa dijo e nang le sefate se setelele bohareng, difate tse nyane, dihlahla, dimela tse emeng hodimo, dimela tse koahelang mobu le semela se nyolohang, metso ya tsona e andang mobung; kganya ya letsatsi e kena ho tloha kgutlong e hodimo ya letshehadi.
items.blindBackTranslation: A cut-away section of a food forest with a tall tree in the middle, small trees, shrubs, upright plants, plants that cover the soil and a climbing plant, their roots spreading in the soil; sunlight enters from the top left corner.

items.sourceEnglish: The Seven Layers: How a Forest Feeds Itself
items.draft: Mekgahlelo e 7: Kamoo Moru o Iphelisang Ka Teng
items.blindBackTranslation: Chapter 7: How a Forest Sustains Itself [?: "Kamoo Moru o Iphelisang Ka Teng" literally "the way a forest/garden feeds/keeps itself alive by it"]. ("Mekgahlelo" = layers/stages; "Mekgahlelo e 7" = The 7 layers/stages.) Literal: "Layers 7: The way the forest keeps itself alive by it"

items.sourceEnglish: Seven planning layers can combine useful plants at different heights
items.draft: Mekgahlelo e supileng ya moralo e ka kopanya dimela tse nang le molemo bophahamong bo fapaneng
items.blindBackTranslation: The seven layers of the plan can combine useful plants at different heights

items.sourceEnglish: Plants can compete for light, water and nutrients
items.draft: Dimela di ka qothisana lehlokwa bakeng sa kganya, metsi le nutrients
items.blindBackTranslation: Plants can compete with one another for light, water and nutrients

items.sourceEnglish: Establishment and ongoing care depend on observed conditions
items.draft: Ho hlongwa le tlhokomelo e tswelang pele di itshetlehile ka maemo a hlokometsweng
items.blindBackTranslation: Establishment and continuing care depend on the conditions observed

items.sourceEnglish: Confirm local suitability before copying any example planting
items.draft: Netefatsa ho tshwaneleha ha sebaka pele o kopitsa mohlala ofe kapa ofe wa ho lema
items.blindBackTranslation: Confirm the suitability of the place before copying any planting example

items.sourceEnglish: Weeds are competing strongly with young lower-layer plants. What should guide the next action?
items.draft: Dimela tse sa batleheng di qothisana lehlokwa haholo le dimela tse nyane tsa mekgahlelo e ka tlase. Ke eng e lokelang ho tataisa ketso e latelang?
items.blindBackTranslation: Unwanted plants are competing strongly with the small plants of the lower layers. What should guide the next action?

items.sourceEnglish: Wait until the fifth year
items.draft: Emela ho fihlela selemo sa bohlano
items.blindBackTranslation: Wait until the fifth year

items.sourceEnglish: Add more plants regardless of water
items.draft: Kenya dimela tse ding ho sa tsotellehe metsi
items.blindBackTranslation: Add other plants regardless of water

items.sourceEnglish: Check the affected plants and manage competition
items.draft: Hlahloba dimela tse amehileng mme o laole tlhodisano
items.blindBackTranslation: Check the affected plants and manage the competition

items.sourceEnglish: Assume all seven layers take care of themselves
items.draft: Nka hore mekgahlelo yohle e supileng e itlhokomela ka boyona
items.blindBackTranslation: Assume that all seven layers take care of themselves

items.sourceEnglish: Observe actual competition and plant condition. A fixed establishment calendar cannot tell you which plants need care now.
items.draft: Hlokomela tlhodisano ya nnete le boemo ba dimela. Kalendara e behilweng ya ho hlongwa e ke ke ya o bolella hore ke dimela dife tse hlokang tlhokomelo hona jwale.
items.blindBackTranslation: Pay attention to the real competition and the condition of the plants. A set calendar of establishment cannot tell you which plants need care now.

items.sourceEnglish: How can leaf litter and shade help protect soil moisture?
items.draft: Leaf litter le moriti di ka thusa jwang ho sireletsa mongobo wa mobu?
items.blindBackTranslation: How can leaf litter and shade help to protect soil moisture?

items.sourceEnglish: They guarantee access to groundwater
items.draft: Di tiisa phihlello ya metsi a ka tlasa lefatshe
items.blindBackTranslation: They secure access to underground water

items.sourceEnglish: They can reduce water loss from the soil surface
items.draft: Di ka fokotsa tahlehelo ya metsi hodima mobu
items.blindBackTranslation: They can reduce loss of water above the soil

items.sourceEnglish: They guarantee higher yield per litre in every system
items.draft: Di tiisa kotulo e kgolo ka litara e nngwe le e nngwe ya metsi tsamaisong efe kapa efe
items.blindBackTranslation: They secure a big harvest per every litre of water in any system

items.sourceEnglish: They remove the need to check watering
items.draft: Di tlosa tlhoko ya ho hlahloba nosetso
items.blindBackTranslation: They remove the need to check irrigation

items.sourceEnglish: Shade and suitable mulch can reduce surface evaporation. Plant water demand and establishment needs still require attention.
items.draft: Moriti le mulch e loketseng di ka fokotsa ho nyamela ha metsi ka mouwane bokaholimong ba mobu. Tlhoko ya metsi ya dimela le ditlhoko tsa ho hlongwa di sa hloka tlhokomelo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Shade and suitable mulch can reduce the disappearance of water by evaporation from the soil surface. The water need of the plants and the needs of establishment still need attention.

items.sourceEnglish: Check local rainfall, frost, heat, soil and water availability before choosing plants.
items.draft: Hlahloba pula ya lehae, serame, motjheso, mobu le phumano ya metsi pele o kgetha dimela.
items.blindBackTranslation: Check local rain, frost, heat, soil and water supply before choosing plants.

items.sourceEnglish: Mango can suffer frost damage. Quince needs suitable winter chilling for reliable cropping.
items.draft: Mango e ka senyeha ke serame. Quince e hloka winter chilling e loketseng e le hore e behe ditholwana ka tshepahalo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Mango can be damaged by frost. Quince needs suitable winter chilling so that it sets fruit reliably.

items.sourceEnglish: A regional label or a sheltered corner is not enough. Confirm each plant and variety with reliable local guidance.
items.draft: Letshwao la sebaka kapa sekgutlo se sireletsehileng ha se lekane. Netefatsa semela se seng le se seng le mofuta ka tataiso e tshepahalang ya lehae.
items.blindBackTranslation: A sign of the place or a sheltered corner is not enough. Confirm each plant and species with reliable local guidance.

items.sourceEnglish: The original list includes pecan, walnut and indigenous fig; apple, pear, plum, black mulberry and loquat; rosemary, Wild Medlar, Cape gooseberry and Barbados cherry.
items.draft: Lenane la pele le kenyelletsa pecan, walnut le indigenous fig; apple, pear, plum, black mulberry le loquat; rosemary, Wild Medlar, Cape gooseberry le Barbados cherry.
items.blindBackTranslation: The first list includes pecan, walnut and indigenous fig; apple, pear, plum, black mulberry and loquat; rosemary, Wild Medlar, Cape gooseberry and Barbados cherry.

items.sourceEnglish: This list is not a blanket recommendation. Check each plant against frost, soil, mature size and the approved local species list.
items.draft: Lenane lena ha se kgothaletso e akaretsang dimela tsohle. Hlahloba semela se seng le se seng ho ya ka serame, mobu, boholo ba ho hola ka botlalo le approved local species list.
items.blindBackTranslation: This list is not a general recommendation for all plants. Check each plant against frost, soil, full-grown size and the approved local species list.

items.sourceEnglish: Keep existing legal and project restrictions in force. Do not plant from a picture alone.
items.draft: Boloka dithibelo tsa molao le tsa projeke tse seng di le teng di sebetsa. O se ke wa jala ka setshwantsho feela.
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep the legal and project restrictions that already exist in force. Do not plant by picture only.

items.sourceEnglish: The original warm-region examples include mango, avocado, Natal Mahogany, banana, pawpaw, litchi, Wild Fig, Barbados cherry and Wild Dagga.
items.draft: Mehlala ya pele ya dibaka tse futhumetseng e kenyelletsa mango, avocado, Natal Mahogany, banana, pawpaw, litchi, Wild Fig, Barbados cherry le Wild Dagga.
items.blindBackTranslation: The first examples of warm places include mango, avocado, Natal Mahogany, banana, pawpaw, litchi, Wild Fig, Barbados cherry and Wild Dagga.

items.sourceEnglish: Marula, Mopane and baobab also appear in the Limpopo examples. Local suitability still needs checking.
items.draft: Marula, Mopane le baobab di hlaha le mehlaleng ya Limpopo. Ho tshwaneleha ha lehae ho sa hloka ho hlahlojwa.
items.blindBackTranslation: Marula, Mopane and baobab also occur in the examples of Limpopo. Local suitability still needs to be checked.

items.sourceEnglish: Useful trees are not automatically edible. Confirm identity and safe use; a landscape photograph is not a food-identification guide.
items.draft: Hore difate di na le molemo ha ho bolele ka boyona hore di ka jewa. Netefatsa hore semela ke sefe le tshebediso e bolokehileng; setshwantsho sa sebaka ha se tataiso ya ho tseba dimela tse jewang.
items.blindBackTranslation: That trees are beneficial does not by itself mean that they can be eaten. Confirm which plant it is and its safe use; a picture of the place is not a guide to identifying edible plants.

items.sourceEnglish: Locally appropriate indigenous plants can support habitat as part of the design.
items.draft: Dimela tsa indigenous tse loketseng sebaka di ka tshehetsa habitat e le karolo ya moralo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Indigenous plants that suit the place can support habitat as part of the design.

items.sourceEnglish: Choose for your ecosystem and the useful role of each plant. There is no sourced percentage target in this lesson.
items.draft: Kgetha bakeng sa ecosystem ya hao le karolo e molemo ya semela se seng le se seng. Ha ho na sepheo sa peresente se nang le mohlodi thutong ena.
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose for your ecosystem and the useful role of each plant. There is no percentage target with a source in this teaching.

items.sourceEnglish: Protect existing natural vegetation. Do not turn healthy grassland into a food forest simply because trees are useful elsewhere.
items.draft: Sireletsa dimela tsa tlhaho tse seng di le teng. O se ke wa fetola naha ya jwang e phetseng hantle hore e be moru wa dijo hobane feela difate di na le molemo dibakeng tse ding.
items.blindBackTranslation: Protect the natural plants that are already there. Do not change a healthy grass land into a food forest just because trees are beneficial in some places.

items.sourceEnglish: A simple shape of South Africa divided into three growing areas by ground colour and terrain alone: a pale high inland plateau with hills, a green humid coastal strip, and a hot red-brown low-lying area. Different tree shapes stand in each.
items.draft: Sebopeho se bonolo sa South Africa se arotsweng dibaka tse tharo tsa kgolo ka mmala wa mobu le sebopeho sa lefatshe feela: sebaka se phahameng se bataletseng sa kahare ho naha se nang le mmala o bosoeu bo bobebe le dithaba tse nyane, lebopo le letala le mongobo, le sebaka se tlase se tjhesang se bofubedu bo bosootho. Dibopeho tse fapaneng tsa difate di eme sebakeng ka seng.
items.blindBackTranslation: A simple shape of South Africa divided into three growth zones by soil colour and landform only: a high flat interior zone with a light white colour and small mountains, a green humid coast, and a hot low zone of brownish red. Different tree shapes stand in each zone.

items.sourceEnglish: Species Selection for South African Food Forests
items.draft: Kgetho ya Mefuta: Meru ya Dijo ya South Africa
items.blindBackTranslation: Choice of Species: Food Forests of South Africa

items.sourceEnglish: Match each plant and variety to the actual site
items.draft: Lekanya semela se seng le se seng le mofuta le sebaka sa nnete
items.blindBackTranslation: Match each plant and species to the real place

items.sourceEnglish: Check identity, safe use and current local restrictions
items.draft: Hlahloba hore semela ke sefe, tshebediso e bolokehileng le dithibelo tsa hajwale tsa lehae
items.blindBackTranslation: Check what the plant is, safe use and the current local restrictions

items.sourceEnglish: A regional example is not approval for every species on its list
items.draft: Mohlala wa sebaka ha se tumello ya mefuta yohle e lenaneng la wona
items.blindBackTranslation: A place example is not permission for all the species on its list

items.sourceEnglish: Use locally appropriate indigenous plants and protect existing natural habitat
items.draft: Sebedisa dimela tsa indigenous tse loketseng sebaka mme o sireletse habitat ya tlhaho e seng e le teng
items.blindBackTranslation: Use indigenous plants that suit the place and protect the natural habitat that already exists

items.sourceEnglish: A grower wants to plant a young mango where hard frost occurs. What risk needs attention?
items.draft: Molemi o batla ho jala mango e nyane moo serame se thata se hlaha teng. Ke kotsi efe e hlokang hlokomelo?
items.blindBackTranslation: A farmer wants to plant a small mango where hard frost occurs. What danger needs attention?

items.sourceEnglish: It thrives — the position offsets frost
items.draft: E ya atleha — sebaka se fokotsa serame
items.blindBackTranslation: It succeeds — the place reduces frost

items.sourceEnglish: It fruits early from the temperature swings
items.draft: E beha ditholwana kapele ka lebaka la ho fetoha ha motjheso
items.blindBackTranslation: It sets fruit early because of the change in heat

items.sourceEnglish: It's likely killed or badly damaged by frost, especially as a young tree
items.draft: Ho na le monyetla wa hore e bolawe kapa e senngwe hampe ke serame, haholoholo e le sefate se sa le senyane
items.blindBackTranslation: There is a chance that it will be killed or badly damaged by frost, especially when it is still a young tree

items.sourceEnglish: It survives with heavy mulch but needs annual replacement
items.draft: E pholoha ka mulch e ngata empa e hloka ho nkelwa sebaka selemo le selemo
items.blindBackTranslation: It survives with a lot of mulch but needs to be replaced place every year [?: "hloka ho nkelwa sebaka" — needs replacing/replanting each year]

items.sourceEnglish: Young mango can be damaged by frost. Check actual site conditions and reliable local guidance rather than assuming a sheltered spot removes the risk.
items.draft: Mango e nyane e ka senyeha ke serame. Hlahloba maemo a nnete a sebaka le tataiso e tshepahalang ya lehae ho e na le ho nka hore sebaka se sireletsehileng se tlosa kotsi.
items.blindBackTranslation: A small mango can be damaged by frost. Check the real conditions of the place and reliable local guidance rather than assuming that a sheltered place removes the danger.

items.sourceEnglish: Why include locally appropriate indigenous plants in a design?
items.draft: Hobaneng ho kenyeletswa dimela tsa indigenous tse loketseng sebaka moralong?
items.blindBackTranslation: Why are indigenous plants that suit the place included in the design?

items.sourceEnglish: They always yield more food per square metre
items.draft: Kamehla di hlahisa dijo tse ngata ka mithara e le nngwe ya sekwere
items.blindBackTranslation: They always produce much food per one square metre

items.sourceEnglish: They can support local habitat, pollinators and other wildlife
items.draft: Di ka tshehetsa habitat ya lehae, pollinators le diphoofolo tse ding tsa naha
items.blindBackTranslation: They can support local habitat, pollinators and other animals of the land

items.sourceEnglish: Every introduced species is illegal
items.draft: Mofuta o mong le o mong o tswang kantle ha o dumellwe ke molao
items.blindBackTranslation: Every species from outside is not permitted by law

items.sourceEnglish: They never need establishment care
items.draft: Ha di hloke tlhokomelo ya ho hlongwa le ka mohla
items.blindBackTranslation: They do not need establishment care ever

items.sourceEnglish: Choose plants for the local ecosystem and their role. This does not establish a universal percentage or remove the need to check suitability.
items.draft: Kgetha dimela bakeng sa ecosystem ya lehae le karolo ya tsona. Sena ha se theha peresente e akaretsang mme ha se tlose tlhoko ya ho hlahloba ho tshwaneleha.
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose plants for the local ecosystem and their role. This does not create a general percentage and does not remove the need to check suitability.

items.sourceEnglish: Start by checking the site, water supply and care available. Protect exposed soil early.
items.draft: Qala ka ho hlahloba sebaka, phepelo ya metsi le tlhokomelo e fumanehang. Sireletsa mobu o pepesitsweng esale pele.
items.blindBackTranslation: Begin by checking the place, the water supply and the care that is available. Protect exposed soil early.

items.sourceEnglish: Temporary support plants may provide shelter and useful cut material where appropriate.
items.draft: Support plants tsa nakwana di ka fana ka setshabelo le thepa e molemo e sehilweng ya dimela moo ho loketseng.
items.blindBackTranslation: Temporary support plants can give shelter and good chopped plant material where suitable.

items.sourceEnglish: Main trees and lower layers can be introduced as conditions allow. Ground cover need not wait until the end; avoid plants competing with young trees.
items.draft: Difate tsa sehlooho le mekgahlelo e ka tlase di ka kenngwa ha maemo a dumela. Dimela tse koahelang mobu ha di hloke ho ema ho fihlela qetellong; qoba dimela tse qothisanang le difate tse nyane.
items.blindBackTranslation: Main trees and lower layers can be added when conditions agree. Plants that cover the ground do not need to wait until the end; avoid plants that compete with small trees.

items.sourceEnglish: Begin with an area you can water and maintain. Check existing vegetation before clearing.
items.draft: Qala ka sebaka seo o ka se nosetsang le ho se hlokomela. Hlahloba dimela tse seng di le teng pele o di tlosa.
items.blindBackTranslation: Begin with a place that you can water and take care of. Check plants that already exist before you remove them.

items.sourceEnglish: Where appropriate, plain cardboard under suitable mulch can suppress unwanted growth. Keep water able to enter the soil and leave trunks clear.
items.draft: Moo ho loketseng, cardboard e tlwaelehileng tlasa mulch e loketseng e ka hatella kgolo e sa batleheng. Dumella metsi hore a kene mobung mme o boloke mebele ya difate e hlakile.
items.blindBackTranslation: Where suitable, plain cardboard under suitable mulch can suppress unwanted growth. Allow water to enter the soil and keep the tree trunks clear.

items.sourceEnglish: Plan spacing from mature plant size. Prepare nursery plants for the next suitable planting opportunity.
items.draft: Rera sebaka ho ya ka boholo ba dimela ha di hole ka botlalo. Lokisetsa nursery plants bakeng sa monyetla o latelang o loketseng wa ho jala.
items.blindBackTranslation: Plan the space according to the size of plants when they have grown fully. Prepare nursery plants for the next suitable opportunity to plant.

items.sourceEnglish: Watch how shade, roots and available water affect neighbouring plants.
items.draft: Sheba kamoo moriti, metso le metsi a fumanehang di amang dimela tse haufi kateng.
items.blindBackTranslation: Watch how shade, roots and available water affect the nearby plants.

items.sourceEnglish: Comfrey and wild garlic appear in the original underplanting example; check their local suitability before use.
items.draft: Comfrey le wild garlic di hlaha mohlaleng wa pele wa dimela tse jetsweng tlasa difate; hlahloba hore na di loketse sebaka pele o di sebedisa.
items.blindBackTranslation: Comfrey and wild garlic appear in the first example of plants planted under trees; check whether they suit the place before you use them.

items.sourceEnglish: Prune or thin support plants when needed, using methods suited to each species. Suitable clean cuttings can return as mulch. Do not wait for a fixed year if competition is already harming plants.
items.draft: Faola kapa etsa thinning ya support plants ha ho hlokahala, o sebedisa mekgwa e loketseng mofuta o mong le o mong. Dikotwana tse hlwekileng tse loketseng di ka kgutlela e le mulch. O se ke wa emela selemo se behilweng haeba tlhodisano e se e senya dimela.
items.blindBackTranslation: Prune or do thinning of support plants when needed, using methods suited to each kind. Clean suitable small pieces can return as mulch. Do not wait for a set year if competition is already damaging the plants.

items.sourceEnglish: Choose a planting opportunity when soil moisture and expected weather support establishment.
items.draft: Kgetha monyetla wa ho lema mohla mongobo wa mobu le maemo a lehodimo a lebelletsweng di tshehetsa ho hlongwa ha dimela.
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose the opportunity to plant on the day when soil moisture and the expected weather conditions support the establishment of the plants.

items.sourceEnglish: Rain can help, but check the root zone and keep a backup watering plan. Avoid planting into waterlogged ground.
items.draft: Pula e ka thusa, empa hlahloba root zone mme o boloke leano la tlatsetso la nosetso. Qoba ho lema mobung o tletseng metsi.
items.blindBackTranslation: Rain can help, but check the root zone and keep a plan for additional irrigation. Avoid planting in waterlogged soil.

items.sourceEnglish: Check young plants after planting. Harvest timing and outside inputs depend on the species, site and care; there is no guaranteed fifth-year result.
items.draft: Hlahloba dimela tse nyane ka mora ho jala. Nako ya kotulo le dintho tse tlisetswang kantle di itshetlehile ka mofuta, sebaka le tlhokomelo; ha ho na sephetho se tiisitsweng sa selemo sa bohlano.
items.blindBackTranslation: Check the small plants after planting. Time of harvest and things brought in from outside depend on the kind, the place and the care; there is no confirmed result of the fifth year.

items.sourceEnglish: The same patch of ground at four stages, left to right: loose mulch being spread over cardboard on soil, then fast low pioneer plants, then young canopy trees with lower layers filling in, and finally a settled layered planting.
items.draft: Sebaka se le seng sa mobu se tshwanang ka dikgato tse nne, ho tloha ka letshehadi ho ya ka le letona: mulch e lokolohileng e hasuwa hodima cardboard mobung, ka mora moo dimela tse tlase tsa pele tse holang ka potlako, ka mora moo difate tsa canopy tse sa le dinyane tse nang le mekgahlelo e ka tlase e ntseng e tlatsa, mme qetellong dimela tse jetsweng ka mekgahlelo tse seng di tsitsitse.
items.blindBackTranslation: One and the same piece of soil in four steps, from left to right: loose mulch spread on top of cardboard on the soil, then the first low fast-growing plants, then young canopy trees with the lower layers filling in, and finally layered plantings that are already stable.

items.sourceEnglish: Establishing a Food Forest: Observe and Adjust
items.draft: Ho Theha Moru wa Dijo: Hlokomela, O Fetole
items.blindBackTranslation: Creating a Food Forest: Observe, and Change

items.sourceEnglish: Protect exposed soil early
items.draft: Sireletsa mobu o pepesilweng esale pele
items.blindBackTranslation: Protect exposed soil early

items.sourceEnglish: Plan the sequence around conditions and available care
items.draft: Rera tatellano ho ya ka maemo le tlhokomelo e fumanehang
items.blindBackTranslation: Plan the order according to conditions and the care available

items.sourceEnglish: Check root-zone moisture even during the rainy season
items.draft: Hlahloba mongobo wa root zone leha e le nakong ya pula
items.blindBackTranslation: Check root zone moisture even in the rainy season

items.sourceEnglish: Manage competition as it develops; harvest dates are not guaranteed
items.draft: Laola tlhodisano ha e ntse e hlaha; matsatsi a kotulo ha a tiiswe
items.blindBackTranslation: Manage competition as it appears; harvest days are not guaranteed

items.sourceEnglish: A farmer puts plain cardboard under suitable mulch where grass is growing. What can it help do?
items.draft: Molemi o beha cardboard e tlwaelehileng tlasa mulch e loketseng moo jwang bo melang teng. E ka thusa ho etsa eng?
items.blindBackTranslation: A farmer puts plain cardboard under suitable mulch where grass grows. What can it help to do?

items.sourceEnglish: Creating a moisture barrier that blocks water from the soil
items.draft: Ho etsa tshitiso ya mongobo e thibelang metsi ho kena mobung
items.blindBackTranslation: To make a moisture barrier that stops water entering the soil

items.sourceEnglish: Block light and help suppress grass while it breaks down; check for regrowth
items.draft: Ho thibela kganya le ho thusa ho hatella jwang ha e ntse e bola; hlahloba hore na bo a mela hape
items.blindBackTranslation: To block light and help suppress grass while it rots; check whether it grows back again

items.sourceEnglish: Providing a stable base so wood chips don't shift
items.draft: Ho fana ka motheo o tsitsitseng e le hore dikotwana tsa patsi di se ke tsa sutha
items.blindBackTranslation: To provide a stable base so that pieces of wood do not slide

items.sourceEnglish: Reflecting heat upward to warm the soil
items.draft: Ho kgutlisetsa motjheso hodimo ho futhumatsa mobu
items.blindBackTranslation: To reflect heat upward to warm the soil

items.sourceEnglish: Cardboard under suitable mulch can block light and reduce grass growth. Existing grass may regrow, so check the area. Keep water able to enter the soil and mulch clear of trunks.
items.draft: Cardboard tlasa mulch e loketseng e ka thibela kganya mme ya fokotsa kgolo ya jwang. Jwang bo seng bo le teng bo ka mela hape, ka hona hlahloba sebaka. Dumella metsi hore a kene mobung mme o boloke mulch hole le mebele ya difate.
items.blindBackTranslation: Cardboard under suitable mulch can block light and reduce the growth of grass. Grass that is already there can grow again, so check the place. Allow water to enter the soil and keep the mulch away from the trunks of trees.

items.sourceEnglish: When should a grower consider pruning or thinning temporary support plants?
items.draft: Molemi o lokela ho nahana neng ka ho faola kapa thinning ya support plants tsa nakwana?
items.blindBackTranslation: When should a farmer think about pruning or thinning temporary support plants?

items.sourceEnglish: Only on a fixed anniversary
items.draft: Feela ka letsatsi le behilweng la selemo le selemo
items.blindBackTranslation: Only on a set day of every year

items.sourceEnglish: When observed competition requires it, using methods suited to the species
items.draft: Ha tlhodisano e hlokometsweng e hloka jwalo, ho sebediswa mekgwa e loketseng mefuta eo ya dimela
items.blindBackTranslation: When observed competition needs it, using methods suited to those kinds of plants

items.sourceEnglish: As soon as any leaf falls
items.draft: Hang ha lekgasi leha e le lefe le wa
items.blindBackTranslation: As soon as any leaf falls

items.sourceEnglish: Never, because support plants cannot compete
items.draft: Le ka mohla, hobane support plants di ke ke tsa qothisana lehlokwa
items.blindBackTranslation: Never, because support plants cannot compete

items.sourceEnglish: Temporary support plants can become competitors. Observe light, water and growth, then choose suitable management rather than relying on a fixed year.
items.draft: Support plants tsa nakwana di ka fetoha dimela tse qothisanang le tse ding. Hlokomela kganya, metsi le kgolo, ebe o kgetha tsamaiso e loketseng ho e na le ho itshetleha ka selemo se behilweng.
items.blindBackTranslation: Temporary support plants can become plants that compete with others. Pay attention to light, water and growth, then choose suitable management rather than depending on a set year.

items.sourceEnglish: Food Forest Design
items.draft: Moralo wa Food Forest
items.blindBackTranslation: Design of a Food Forest

items.sourceEnglish: Build a living food system in layers.
items.draft: Haha tsamaiso ya dijo e phelang ka mekgahlelo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Build a food system that lives in stages.

items.sourceEnglish: Grow food from tall canopy down to root crops.
items.draft: Lema dijo ho tloha ho canopy e telele ho isa ho dijalo tsa metso.
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant food from the tall canopy down to the root crops.

items.sourceEnglish: Use vertical space, soil life, shade, and moisture together.
items.draft: Sebedisa sebaka sa bophahamo, bophelo ba mobu, moriti le mongobo hammoho.
items.blindBackTranslation: Use the space of height, the life of the soil, shade and moisture together.

items.sourceEnglish: Learn how to design and establish a food forest for your farm.
items.draft: Ithute ho rala le ho qala food forest polasing ya hao.
items.blindBackTranslation: Learn to design and to start a food forest on your farm.

items.sourceEnglish: Why This Matters
items.draft: Hobaneng Sena se le Bohlokwa
items.blindBackTranslation: Why This Is Important

items.sourceEnglish: A food forest grows useful plants at different heights.
items.draft: Food forest e hodisa dimela tse molemo bophahamong bo fapaneng.
items.blindBackTranslation: A food forest grows good plants at different heights.

items.sourceEnglish: Good design can combine harvests, shade and soil cover. Plants still compete for light, water and nutrients.
items.draft: Moralo o motle o ka kopanya dikotulo, moriti le sekwahelo sa mobu. Dimela di ntse di phehisana ka kganya, metsi le nutrients.
items.blindBackTranslation: A good design can combine harvests, shade and soil cover. Plants keep competing for light, water and nutrients.

items.sourceEnglish: Plan the care you can provide and watch how the planting changes.
items.draft: Rala tlhokomelo eo o ka e fanang mme o shebe hore dimela di fetoha jwang.
items.blindBackTranslation: Design the care that you can give, and watch how the plants change.

items.sourceEnglish: Learning Outcomes
items.draft: Seo O Tla Ithutang Sona
items.blindBackTranslation: What You Will Learn

items.sourceEnglish: Name the seven commonly described food-forest layers.
items.draft: Reha mekgahlelo e 7 ya food forest e hlalosoang hangata.
items.blindBackTranslation: Name the 7 layers of a food forest that are commonly described.

items.sourceEnglish: Check plants against your site, local ecology and the approved project list.
items.draft: Hlahloba dimela ho ya ka sebaka sa hao, tlhaho ya sebaka le lenane le amohetsweng la projeke.
items.blindBackTranslation: Check plants according to your place, the nature of the place, and the approved list of the project.

items.sourceEnglish: Plan establishment and ongoing care without assuming a fixed date for harvest or canopy closure.
items.draft: Rala nako ya pele kamora ho jala (establishment) le tlhokomelo e tswelang pele, ntle le ho nka hore ho na le letsatsi le tsitsitseng la kotulo kapa la ho kwalana ha canopy.
items.blindBackTranslation: Plan the early period after planting and the ongoing care, without assuming that there is a fixed day of harvest or of the canopy closing.

items.sourceEnglish: The Forest Uses Every Layer
items.draft: Moru o Sebedisa Mokgahlelo o Mong le o Mong
items.blindBackTranslation: The Forest Uses Every Layer

items.sourceEnglish: An indigenous forest fills the space from the highest branches to the roots.
items.draft: Moru wa indigenous o tlatsa sebaka ho tloha makaleng a hodimo ho isa metsong.
items.blindBackTranslation: An indigenous forest fills the space from the upper branches down to the roots.

items.sourceEnglish: Different plants use the light and moisture available at their level.
items.draft: Dimela tse fapaneng di sebedisa kganya le mongobo tse fumanehang boemong ba tsona.
items.blindBackTranslation: Different plants use the light and moisture that are found at their position.

items.sourceEnglish: A food forest copies this pattern with productive species.
items.draft: Food forest e etsisa mokgwa ona ka mefuta e hlahisang.
items.blindBackTranslation: A food forest imitates this way with producing species.

items.sourceEnglish: The result is not one crop in one row, but many useful layers growing together.
items.draft: Phello ha se sejalo se le seng moleng o le mong, empa ke mekgahlelo (layers) e mengata e molemo e melang hammoho.
items.blindBackTranslation: The result is not one crop in one row, but many good layers (layers) growing together.

items.sourceEnglish: Watch: Read the Seven Planting Layers
items.draft: Sheba: Bala Mekgahlelo e 7 ya ho Jala
items.blindBackTranslation: Look: Count the 7 Layers of Planting

items.sourceEnglish: Find seven planting layers.
items.draft: Fumana mekgahlelo e 7 ya ho jala.
items.blindBackTranslation: Find the 7 layers of planting.

items.sourceEnglish: Tall trees form the canopy.
items.draft: Difate tse telele di etsa canopy.
items.blindBackTranslation: Tall trees make the canopy.

items.sourceEnglish: Smaller trees grow below it.
items.draft: Difate tse nyane di mela ka tlasa canopy.
items.blindBackTranslation: Small trees grow below the canopy.

items.sourceEnglish: Then look for woody shrubs.
items.draft: Ebe o batla dihlahla tse nang le lehong.
items.blindBackTranslation: Then look for shrubs that have wood.

items.sourceEnglish: Herbaceous plants have soft stems.
items.draft: Dimela tsa herbaceous di na le dikutu tse bonolo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Herbaceous plants have soft stems.

items.sourceEnglish: Ground cover spreads across the surface.
items.draft: Dimela tse kwahelang mobu (ground cover) di hasana hodima mobu.
items.blindBackTranslation: Plants that cover the soil (ground cover) spread over the soil.

items.sourceEnglish: Root crops grow below the surface.
items.draft: Dijalo tsa metso (root crops) di mela ka tlasa bokahodimo ba mobu.
items.blindBackTranslation: Crops of roots (root crops) grow below the surface of the soil.

items.sourceEnglish: Climbers use suitable supports.
items.draft: Dimela tse hloang di sebedisa dintho tse loketseng tse di tshehetsang.
items.blindBackTranslation: Plants that grow [?: climbing/that sprout] use suitable things [?dintho: things/materials] that support them.

items.sourceEnglish: These are planning layers, not fixed height bands. Choose plants and spacing for your site.
items.draft: Tsena ke mekgahlelo ya moralo, e seng dibande tse tsitsitseng tsa bophahamo. Kgetha dimela le sebaka pakeng tsa tsona bakeng sa sebaka sa hao.
items.blindBackTranslation: These are layers of the design, not fixed bands of height. Choose plants and the space between them for your place.

items.sourceEnglish: The Seven Layers
items.draft: Mekgahlelo e 7
items.blindBackTranslation: The 7 Layers

items.sourceEnglish: Think of tall canopy, smaller trees, shrubs and herbaceous plants.
items.draft: Nahana ka canopy e telele, difate tse nyane, dihlahla le dimela tsa herbaceous.
items.blindBackTranslation: Think of a tall canopy, small trees, shrubs and herbaceous plants.

items.sourceEnglish: Ground cover protects the surface, root crops grow below it, and climbers use suitable supports.
items.draft: Dimela tse kwahelang mobu di sireletsa bokahodimo ba mobu, dijalo tsa metso di mela ka tlasa bokahodimo boo, mme dimela tse hloang di sebedisa ditshehetso tse loketseng.
items.blindBackTranslation: Plants that cover the soil protect the surface of the soil, crops of roots grow below that surface, and plants that climb use suitable supports.

items.sourceEnglish: The heights and spacing depend on the plants and site. These are planning layers, not fixed height bands.
items.draft: Bophahamo le sebaka pakeng tsa dimela di ipapisitse le dimela le sebaka. Tsena ke mekgahlelo ya moralo, e seng dibande tse tsitsitseng tsa bophahamo.
items.blindBackTranslation: The height and the space between plants depend on the plants and the place. These are layers of the design, not fixed bands of height.

items.sourceEnglish: Read a Layered Planting Example
items.draft: Bala Mohlala wa ho Jala ka Mekgahlelo
items.blindBackTranslation: Read an Example of Planting in Layers

items.sourceEnglish: The original Highveld example includes Wild Fig or pecan above lemon, naartjie and black mulberry.
items.draft: Mohlala wa pele wa Highveld o kenyeletsa Wild Fig kapa pecan hodima lemon, naartjie le black mulberry.
items.blindBackTranslation: A first example of the Highveld includes Wild Fig or pecan above lemon, naartjie and black mulberry.

items.sourceEnglish: It places Cape gooseberry and Wild Medlar with vegetables, wild garlic, sweet potato and granadilla.
items.draft: O beha Cape gooseberry le Wild Medlar hammoho le merogo, wild garlic, sweet potato le granadilla.
items.blindBackTranslation: It puts Cape gooseberry and Wild Medlar together with vegetables, wild garlic, sweet potato and granadilla.

items.sourceEnglish: Treat this as a layout example, not permission to plant every species. Check identity, frost tolerance, mature size and local restrictions first.
items.draft: Nka sena e le mohlala wa moralo, e seng tumello ya ho jala mofuta o mong le o mong. Pele, hlahloba hore semela ke sefe, frost tolerance, boholo ba ho hola ka botlalo le dithibelo tsa sebaka.
items.blindBackTranslation: Take this as an example of a design, not a permission to plant every species. First, check which plant it is, frost tolerance, size of full growth and the restrictions of the place.

items.sourceEnglish: Care Changes as Plants Grow
items.draft: Tlhokomelo e a fetoha ha dimela di ntse di hola.
items.blindBackTranslation: Care changes as plants grow.

items.sourceEnglish: Young plants need establishment care: moisture checks, weed control and protection from damage.
items.draft: Dimela tse nyane di hloka tlhokomelo ya nako ya pele kamora ho jala (establishment care): ho hlahloba mongobo, ho laola dimela tse sa batleheng le ho di sireletsa tshenyong.
items.blindBackTranslation: Small plants need care in the early period after planting (establishment care): checking moisture, controlling unwanted plants and protecting them from damage.

items.sourceEnglish: As plants grow, shade and leaf litter change conditions below them.
items.draft: Ha dimela di ntse di hola, moriti le leaf litter di fetola maemo a ka tlase ho tsona.
items.blindBackTranslation: As plants grow, shade and leaf litter change the conditions beneath them.

items.sourceEnglish: Check competition and access. Prune, thin or adjust lower planting when observations call for it; the system does not become care-free on a fixed birthday.
items.draft: Hlahloba ho phehisana le phihlello. Seha makala, kapa etsa thinning, kapa lokisa dimela tsa ka tlase, ha seo o se bonang se hloka jwalo; tsamaiso ha e fetohe e se hloke tlhokomelo ka letsatsi le tsitsitseng la tswalo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Check competition and access [?phihlello: access/reach/light]. Prune branches [Seha makala: cut branches], or do thinning, or tidy the understory plants [dimela tsa ka tlase: plants below/under], when what you see needs it; the system does not become one that needs no care on a fixed day of birth [?letsatsi le tsitsitseng la tswalo: fixed/steady day of birth].

items.sourceEnglish: Choose for Your Site
items.draft: Kgetha ho ya ka Sebaka sa Hao
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose According to Your Place

items.sourceEnglish: Check local rainfall, frost, heat, soil and water availability before choosing plants.
items.draft: Hlahloba pula ya sebaka, serame, mocheso, mobu le ho fumaneha ha metsi pele o kgetha dimela.
items.blindBackTranslation: Check the rain of the place, frost, heat, soil and the availability of water before you choose plants.

items.sourceEnglish: Mango can suffer frost damage. Quince needs suitable winter chilling for reliable cropping.
items.draft: Mango e ka senyehela ke serame. Quince e hloka winter chilling e loketseng bakeng sa kotulo e tshepehang.
items.blindBackTranslation: Mango can be damaged by frost. Quince needs suitable winter chilling for a reliable harvest.

items.sourceEnglish: A regional label or a sheltered corner is not enough. Confirm each plant and variety with reliable local guidance.
items.draft: Lebitso la sebaka kapa sekgutlo se sirelelitsweng ha di lekane. Netefatsa semela se seng le se seng le mofuta ka tataiso e tshepehang ya sebaka.
items.blindBackTranslation: The name of the place or a sheltered corner are not enough. Confirm each plant and species with reliable guidance for the place.

items.sourceEnglish: Watch: Match the Species to the Climate
items.draft: Sheba: Lekanya Mefuta le Boemo ba Leholimo
items.blindBackTranslation: Look: Match Species and Climate

items.sourceEnglish: Climate decides which species belong.
items.draft: Boemo ba leholimo bo etsa qeto ya hore ke mefuta efe e loketseng.
items.blindBackTranslation: Climate decides which species are suitable.

items.sourceEnglish: On the Highveld, choose cold-tolerant trees and shrubs; on the KZN coast and Lowveld, choose warm-climate species.
items.draft: Highveld, kgetha difate le dihlahla tse mamellang bophodisa; KZN coast le Lowveld, kgetha mefuta ya dibaka tse mofuthu.
items.blindBackTranslation: Highveld, choose trees and shrubs that tolerate cold; KZN coast and Lowveld, choose species of warm places.

items.sourceEnglish: Match every plant to your site.
items.draft: Lekanya semela se seng le se seng le sebaka sa hao.
items.blindBackTranslation: Match each plant with your place.

items.sourceEnglish: Check the Highveld Examples
items.draft: Hlahloba Mehlala ya Highveld
items.blindBackTranslation: Check Examples of the Highveld

items.sourceEnglish: The original list includes pecan, walnut and indigenous fig; apple, pear, plum, black mulberry and loquat; rosemary, Wild Medlar, Cape gooseberry and Barbados cherry.
items.draft: Lenane la pele le kenyeletsa pecan, walnut le indigenous fig; apple, pear, plum, black mulberry le loquat; rosemary, Wild Medlar, Cape gooseberry le Barbados cherry.
items.blindBackTranslation: The first list includes pecan, walnut and indigenous fig; apple, pear, plum, black mulberry and loquat; rosemary, Wild Medlar, Cape gooseberry and Barbados cherry.

items.sourceEnglish: This list is not a blanket recommendation. Check each plant against frost, soil, mature size and the approved local species list.
items.draft: Lenane lena ha se tlhahiso e sebetsang dibakeng tsohle. Hlahloba semela se seng le se seng ho latela serame, mobu, boholo ba ho hola ka botlalo le approved local species list.
items.blindBackTranslation: This list is not a recommendation that works in all places. Check each plant according to frost, soil, size of growing fully and the approved local species list.

items.sourceEnglish: Keep existing legal and project restrictions in force. Do not plant from a picture alone.
items.draft: Boloka dithibelo tse teng tsa molao le tsa projeke di sebetsa. O se ke wa jala ka ho sheba setshwantsho feela.
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep the existing restrictions of law and of the project in force. Do not plant by looking at a picture only.

items.sourceEnglish: Check the Warm-Region Examples
items.draft: Hlahloba Mehlala ya Dibaka tse Mofuthu
items.blindBackTranslation: Check Examples of Warm Places

items.sourceEnglish: The original warm-region examples include mango, avocado, Natal Mahogany, banana, pawpaw, litchi, Wild Fig, Barbados cherry and Wild Dagga.
items.draft: Mehlala ya pele ya dibaka tse mofuthu e kenyeletsa mango, avocado, Natal Mahogany, banana, pawpaw, litchi, Wild Fig, Barbados cherry le Wild Dagga.
items.blindBackTranslation: First examples of warm places include mango, avocado, Natal Mahogany, banana, pawpaw, litchi, Wild Fig, Barbados cherry and Wild Dagga.

items.sourceEnglish: Marula, Mopane and baobab also appear in the Limpopo examples. Local suitability still needs checking.
items.draft: Marula, Mopane le baobab le tsona di hlaha mehlaleng ya Limpopo. Hore na di loketse sebaka ho sa hloka ho hlahlojwa.
items.blindBackTranslation: Marula, Mopane and baobab also appear in the examples of Limpopo. Whether they are suitable for the place still needs to be checked.

items.sourceEnglish: Useful trees are not automatically edible. Confirm identity and safe use; a landscape photograph is not a food-identification guide.
items.draft: Hore difate di na le molemo ha ho bolele hore di ka jewa. Netefatsa hore ke sefe le tshebediso e bolokehileng; setshwantsho sa naha ha se tataiso ya ho tseba hore ke dijo dife.
items.blindBackTranslation: Even though trees have benefit, it does not mean that they can be eaten. Confirm which one it is and its safe use; a picture of the land is not a guide to knowing which are foods.

items.sourceEnglish: Include Locally Appropriate Indigenous Plants
items.draft: Kenya Dimela tsa Indigenous tse Loketseng Sebaka
items.blindBackTranslation: Bring in Indigenous Plants Suitable for the Place

items.sourceEnglish: Locally appropriate indigenous plants can support habitat as part of the design.
items.draft: Dimela tsa indigenous tse loketseng sebaka sa heno di ka tshehetsa habitat e le karolo ya moralo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Indigenous plants suitable for your place can support habitat as a part of the design.

items.sourceEnglish: Choose for your ecosystem and the useful role of each plant. There is no sourced percentage target in this lesson.
items.draft: Kgetha ho latela ecosystem ya hao le tshebetso e molemo ya semela se seng le se seng. Thutong ena ha ho na nepo ya diperesente e nang le mohlodi.
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose according to your ecosystem and the good function of each plant. In this course there is no percentage target that has a source.

items.sourceEnglish: Protect existing natural vegetation. Do not turn healthy grassland into a food forest simply because trees are useful elsewhere.
items.draft: Sireletsa dimela tsa tlhaho tse teng. O se ke wa fetola naha ya joang e phetseng hantle hore e be food forest feela ka lebaka la hore difate di na le molemo dibakeng tse ding.
items.blindBackTranslation: Protect the natural plants that are already there. Do not change grassland that is living/growing well [?healthy] so that it becomes a food forest only because trees have benefit in other places.

items.sourceEnglish: Plan the Sequence for the Site
items.draft: Rala Tatellano bakeng sa Sebaka
items.blindBackTranslation: Design a Sequence for the Place

items.sourceEnglish: Start by checking the site, water supply and care available. Protect exposed soil early.
items.draft: Qala ka ho hlahloba sebaka, tlhahiso ya metsi le tlhokomelo e teng. Sireletsa mobu o pepeneneng kapele.
items.blindBackTranslation: Start by checking the place, the supply of water and the care that is there. Protect bare soil quickly.

items.sourceEnglish: Temporary support plants may provide shelter and useful cut material where appropriate.
items.draft: Support plants tsa nakwana di ka fana ka tshireletso le thepa e sehilweng e sebetsang moo ho loketseng.
items.blindBackTranslation: Temporary support plants can give protection and cut material that works where suitable.

items.sourceEnglish: Main trees and lower layers can be introduced as conditions allow. Ground cover need not wait until the end; avoid plants competing with young trees.
items.draft: Difate tse ka sehlooho le mekgahlelo e ka tlase di ka kenngwa ha maemo a dumella. Dimela tse kwahelang mobu ha di hloke ho emela ho fihlela qetellong; qoba hore dimela di phehisane le difate tse nyane.
items.blindBackTranslation: Main trees and the lower layers can be put in when conditions allow. Plants that cover the soil do not need to wait until the end; avoid having plants compete with small trees.

items.sourceEnglish: Watch: Care for a Young Food Forest
items.draft: Sheba: Hlokomela Food Forest e Sa Tswa Jalwa
items.blindBackTranslation: Look: Care for a Newly Planted Food Forest

items.sourceEnglish: This picture shows a young food forest. Start with an area you can care for.
items.draft: Setshwantsho sena se bontsha food forest e sa le nyane. Qala ka sebaka seo o ka se hlokomelang.
items.blindBackTranslation: This picture shows a food forest that is still small. Start with a place that you can look after.

items.sourceEnglish: Protect exposed soil early. Here, loose mulch covers the soil.
items.draft: Sireletsa mobu o pepeneneng kapele. Mona, mulch e lokolohileng e kwahela mobu.
items.blindBackTranslation: Protect bare soil quickly. Here, loose mulch covers the soil.

items.sourceEnglish: Keep mulch away from the trunk. Notice the clear space at the tree's base.
items.draft: Boloka mulch kgole le kutu ya sefate. Sheba sebaka se hlakileng botlaseng ba sefate.
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep mulch far from the trunk of the tree. Look at the clear space at the bottom of the tree.

items.sourceEnglish: Watch for competition. The farmer is removing grass near the young tree.
items.draft: Elellwa ho phehisana. Molemi o tlosa joang haufi le sefate se senyane.
items.blindBackTranslation: Be aware of competition. The farmer removes grass near the small tree.

items.sourceEnglish: Before adding more plants, check moisture, shelter and the care you can provide. Let what you observe guide your next step.
items.draft: Pele o eketsa dimela tse ding, hlahloba mongobo, tshireletso le tlhokomelo eo o ka e fanang. Tlohela seo o se bonang se tataise mohato o latelang.
items.blindBackTranslation: Before you add other plants, check moisture, protection and the care you can give. Let what you see guide the next step.

items.sourceEnglish: Prepare a Manageable First Area
items.draft: Lokisa Sebaka sa Pele se Laolehang
items.blindBackTranslation: Prepare a Manageable First Area

items.sourceEnglish: Begin with an area you can water and maintain. Check existing vegetation before clearing.
items.draft: Qala ka sebaka seo o ka se nosetsang le ho se hlokomela. Hlahloba dimela tse teng pele o di tlosa.
items.blindBackTranslation: Start with an area that you can water and care for. Check the plants that are there before you remove them.

items.sourceEnglish: Where appropriate, plain cardboard under suitable mulch can suppress unwanted growth. Keep water able to enter the soil and leave trunks clear.
items.draft: Moo ho loketseng, cardboard e se nang kgatiso ka tlasa mulch e loketseng e ka thiba kgolo e sa batleheng. Dumella metsi hore a kene mobung mme o tlohele dikutu di hlakile.
items.blindBackTranslation: Where suitable, cardboard without printing below suitable mulch can block unwanted growth. Allow water to enter the soil and leave the stems clear.

items.sourceEnglish: Plan spacing from mature plant size. Prepare nursery plants for the next suitable planting opportunity.
items.draft: Rala sebaka pakeng tsa dimela ho latela boholo ba tsona ha di hola ka botlalo. Lokisa nursery plants bakeng sa monyetla o latelang o loketseng wa ho jala.
items.blindBackTranslation: Plan the space between plants according to their size when they have grown fully. Prepare nursery plants for the next suitable opportunity of planting.

items.sourceEnglish: Adjust as the Trees Grow
items.draft: Fetola ha Difate di Ntse di Hola
items.blindBackTranslation: Adjust as the Trees Grow

items.sourceEnglish: Watch how shade, roots and available water affect neighbouring plants.
items.draft: Elellwa hore moriti, metso le metsi a teng di ama jwang dimela tse haufi.
items.blindBackTranslation: Be aware of how shade, roots and the water that is there affect nearby plants.

items.sourceEnglish: Comfrey and wild garlic appear in the original underplanting example; check their local suitability before use.
items.draft: Comfrey le wild garlic di hlaha mohlalong wa pele wa dimela tse jetsweng ka tlasa difate; hlahloba hore na di loketse sebaka pele o di sebedisa.
items.blindBackTranslation: Comfrey and wild garlic appear in the first example of plants planted below trees; check whether they suit the place before you use them.

items.sourceEnglish: Prune or thin support plants when needed, using methods suited to each species. Suitable clean cuttings can return as mulch. Do not wait for a fixed year if competition is already harming plants.
items.draft: Seha makala kapa etsa thinning ya support plants ha ho hlokeha, o sebedisa mekgwa e loketseng mofuta o mong le o mong. Makala a sehilweng a hlwekileng a loketseng a ka kgutlela e le mulch. O se ke wa emela selemo se tsitsitseng haeba ho phehisana ho se ho senya dimela.
items.blindBackTranslation: Cut branches or do thinning of support plants when needed, using methods suitable to each species. Clean cut branches that are suitable can return as mulch. Do not wait for a fixed year if competition is already damaging plants.

items.sourceEnglish: Plant with Reliable Moisture
items.draft: Jala ha Mongobo o Tshepehile
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant When Moisture Is Reliable

items.sourceEnglish: Choose a planting opportunity when soil moisture and expected weather support establishment.
items.draft: Kgetha monyetla wa ho jala ha mongobo wa mobu le maemo a leholimo a lebelletsweng a thusa nako ya pele kamora ho jala (establishment).
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose an opportunity of planting where the moisture of the soil and the expected conditions of the weather help the early period after planting.

items.sourceEnglish: Rain can help, but check the root zone and keep a backup watering plan. Avoid planting into waterlogged ground.
items.draft: Pula e ka thusa, empa hlahloba root zone mme o boloke leano la bobedi la ho nosetsa. Qoba ho jala mobung o tletseng metsi.
items.blindBackTranslation: Rain can help, but check the root zone and keep a second plan of watering. Avoid planting in soil that is full of water.

items.sourceEnglish: Check young plants after planting. Harvest timing and outside inputs depend on the species, site and care; there is no guaranteed fifth-year result.
items.draft: Hlahloba dimela tse nyane kamora ho jala. Nako ya kotulo le dintho tse tswang kantle di ipapisitse le mofuta, sebaka le tlhokomelo; ha ho na tiisetso ya sephetho selemong sa bohlano.
items.blindBackTranslation: Check the small plants after planting. Harvest time and things that come from outside depend on the kind, the place and the care; there is no guarantee of a result in the fifth year.

items.sourceEnglish: Field Assignment
items.draft: Mosebetsi wa Tshimong
items.blindBackTranslation: Work in the Field

items.sourceEnglish: Draw the layers for your own proposed planting. Mark access, water and existing natural vegetation.
items.draft: Taka mekgahlelo bakeng sa ho jala hoo o ho rerileng. Tshwaya phihlello, metsi le dimela tsa tlhaho tse teng.
items.blindBackTranslation: Draw layers for the planting that you have planned. Mark access, water and the natural plants that are there.

items.sourceEnglish: Record local frost, rain, soil and available care.
items.draft: Ngola serame, pula, mobu le tlhokomelo e fumanehang sebakeng sa heno.
items.blindBackTranslation: Write down frost, rain, soil and care that are available in your place.

items.sourceEnglish: For each plant from the approved list, record its intended role and the local advice still needed before planting.
items.draft: Bakeng sa semela se seng le se seng lenaneng le dumeletsweng, ngola tshebetso eo se e reretsweng le keletso e amanang le sebaka sa heno e ntseng e hlokeha pele o jala.
items.blindBackTranslation: For each plant in the permitted list, write the function it is intended for and the advice related to your place/area that is still needed before you plant.

items.sourceEnglish: Field Action
items.draft: Ketso ya Tshimong
items.blindBackTranslation: Action in the Field

items.sourceEnglish: Inspect a manageable area and choose one next step.
items.draft: Hlahloba karolo ya sebaka seo o ka se hlokomelang, ebe o kgetha mohato o le mong o latelang.
items.blindBackTranslation: Check the part of the place that you can care for, then choose one next step.

items.sourceEnglish: Protect exposed soil, check plant suitability, or prepare nursery plants.
items.draft: Sireletsa mobu o pepeneneng, hlahloba hore dimela di loketse sebaka, kapa lokisa dimela tsa nursery.
items.blindBackTranslation: Protect bare soil, check that plants suit the place, or prepare nursery plants.

items.sourceEnglish: Plant only when conditions and follow-up care are suitable. Return to the same spot to check survival, soil moisture and competition.
items.draft: Jala feela ha maemo le tlhokomelo e latelang di loketse. Kgutlela sebakeng se le seng ho hlahloba hore na dimela di phetse, mongobo wa mobu le ho phehisana.
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant only when conditions and the care that follows are suitable. Return to the same place to check whether the plants are alive, the moisture of the soil and competition.
